newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Tunisian PM to visit Jordan for cooperation talks.
newsitem.headline: Tunisian PM to visit Jordan for cooperation talks.

text.p: Tunisian Prime Minister Hamed Karoui is expected to leave for Jordan next Sunday for a three-day visit for talks on boosting cooperation between the two countries, official sources said on Wednesday.
Karoui will chair with his Jordanian counterpart Abdul-Karim al-Kabariti the joint commission for cooperation, they added.
Tunisian exports to Jordan dropped sharply to 1.6 million dinars in 1995 from 14.4 million dinars in 1994. Imports from Jordan rose to 5.2 million dinars in 1995 from 4.7 million dinars in 1994.
Tunisia and Jordan in April last year signed five accords for economic cooperation at the end of the first meeting of the joint commission in Tunis.
The accords signed were related to economic, trading, scientific and technical fields, agriculture, maritime transport, tourism and guarantee of investments.
They were aimed at replacing the bilateral preferential trade agreement signed in 1981 which was invalidated from January 1, 1996 to comply with world trade rules banning preferential accords.
Tunisia used to export olive oil, fertilisers, plastic products and ceramics to Jordan and import pharmaceuticals and potassium. ($=one dinar)
